The other shape —
If shape it might be called that shape had none
Distinguishable in member, joint, or limb
Or substance might be called that shadow seemed,
For each seemed either — black it stood as Night . . .

 3–4. As Grabo (1930) 87 has shown, S. attributes to Demogorgon the properties of infra-red rays as
discovered by Herschel in 1800; GM argues that Demogorgon emits infra-red rays ‘because he is
extremely hot; too hot to be visible. It was known, in Herschel’s own words on the solar spectrum, that
“the full red still falls short of the maximum of heat; which perhaps lies even beyond visible refraction”.
 Demogorgon is, in fact, realised in terms of molten magma, the obscure and terrible volcanic agent
